decisive_items: extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma of the left foot treated 9 years earlier
Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a mass arising from the right frontal diploic space
Noncontrast head CT revealed a lytic lesion of the right frontal bone with hypodense soft‐tissue extension into the scalp
response.rationale: History of extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma with a new lytic frontal calvarial mass with intracranial extension is most consistent with metastasis; primary chondrosarcoma is less likely given prior sarcoma and typical metastatic pattern.

rejected.why: Skull chordoma typically midline/clival, not frontal diploic; prior EMC history makes metastasis more likely.
Trauma was minor and preceded by 1 year; lesion is progressive and destructive, not a traumatic lesion.
Plasmacytoma is a possibility but lacks prior EMC context and characteristic imaging features; metastasis is more parsimonious.
Giant cell tumor of skull has different demographics/imaging; prior EMC strongly favors metastasis.
No radiation history to forehead; prior chemotherapy not radiation, and lesion is within prior tumor histology spectrum.
Too nonspecific; metastatic EMC is the specific entity.
Disproved by imaging showing lytic diploic mass; lipoma does not erode bone.
Too broad; EMC is a specific soft tissue sarcoma with known metastatic tendency.
Primary osteosarcoma lacks supporting history and contradicted by prior EMC; metastatic EMC fits better.
